paper_title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
core_problem: Language models exhibit remarkable abilities to solve new tasks from few examples or textual instructions, especially at scale, but paradoxically struggle with basic functionality such as arithmetic or factual lookup where much simpler and smaller models excel. Inherent limitations include inability to access up-to-date information on recent events, tendency to hallucinate facts, difficulties in understanding low-resource languages, lack of mathematical skills to perform precise calculations, and unawareness of the progression of time.
methodology_summary: Toolformer is trained to decide which APIs to call, when to call them, what arguments to pass, and how to best incorporate the results into future token prediction. Training is self-supervised and requires nothing more than a handful of demonstrations for each API. A range of tools is incorporated including a calculator, a Q&A system, a search engine, a translation system, and a calendar.
empirical_results: Toolformer achieves substantially improved zero-shot performance across a variety of downstream tasks, often competitive with much larger models, without sacrificing its core language modeling abilities. Toolformer still lags behind the much larger GPT-3 175B model.
explicit_limitations: Toolformer still lags behind the much larger GPT-3 175B model, likely due to both the simplicity of the search implementation. Existing approaches to tool use either rely on large amounts of human annotations or limit tool use to task-specific settings only, hindering widespread adoption. Underlying LM limitations remain, including inability to access up-to-date information, tendency to hallucinate facts, difficulties with low-resource languages, lack of mathematical skills for precise calculations, and unawareness of time progression.
